title: The current bottleneck is political will, not research
description: Concise case for this being the most important area to work on.

title: An Activist View of AI Governance
description: Longer overview of US-focused AI political advocacy and how it fits into high-level political strategy.

title: The Invisible Side of AI Governance
description: Overview of “insider” vs “outsider” political advocacy work.

title: What We Learned from Briefing 140+ Lawmakers on the Threat from AI
Global Call for AI Red Lines
description: Campaign for promoting international AI governance. The FAQ is useful for info on progress that's been made thus far and what still needs to happen in AI international governance.

title: AI 2040
description: Useful for thinking about how policy decisions fit into long-term future of AI development, although many of the proposals are likely too politically infeasible to aim for in practice.

title: How Should the US Prepare for Increasingly Automated AI R&D?
description: "Low-regret" AI policy proposals, more feasible in the near-term even despite existential risk skepticism.

title: Stop Donating to AI Safety Research*
description: Strong case for donating to political advocacy groups, has detailed information about several.

title: Where I Am Donating in 2025
description: Author gives his high-level analysis for where to donate given his goals and what seems most cost-effective for reaching them and decides on PauseAI US. Useful for thinking about cost-effectiveness and high-level strategy.

title: How to Actually Spend Billions on AI Safety
description: Overview of the main high-level funding bottlenecks in addressing AI risk (mostly political advocacy related), has many concrete ideas to build off of.

title: AI safety needs a moonshot comms initiative
Speaking to Congressional staffers about AI risk
Which AI harms & risks will mobilise the public to act?
description: Many harms from AI have varying degrees of salience among the public and degree to which they are helpful for policy solutions that mitigate existential risk; this paper suggests autonomous warfare strikes the best balance and explores several others.
